sub-01/ieeg/sub-01_coordsystem.json.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: Electrode positions as reported in Brain Treebank's localization.zip, file 'localization/sub_<id>/depth-wm.csv'. The CSV was produced by iELVis (Groppe et al. 2017) + BioImageSuite after co-registering a post-operative fluoroscopy scan to the pre-operative T1 MRI. The axes are labelled L, I, P in the source CSV (presumably Left, Inferior, Posterior), and anatomical region labels come from FreeSurfer parcellations (Desikan-Killiany, Destrieux, DKT) included as extra columns in electrodes.tsv. IMPORTANT: the Brain Treebank release does NOT publish the coordinate units, origin, or the transform to a standard template (MNI, ACPC, ScanRAS, or FreeSurfer surface RAS). Users requiring cross-subject alignment or millimetre distances should consult the original Brain Treebank publication and code release, and/or contact the authors for the co-registration matrices. These coordinates are provided as-is from depth-wm.csv for reproducibility; no transform has been applied in this dataset.
sub-01/ieeg/sub-01_coordsystem.json.iEEGCoordinateProcessingDescription: Post-operative fluoroscopy scan co-registered to pre-operative T1 MRI using iELVis. Electrodes manually identified in BioImageSuite and assigned to FreeSurfer atlases (Desikan-Killiany, Destrieux, DKT). For electrodes located in white matter, contacts were projected to the nearest grey/white matter boundary — the 'ShiftDist' column in the source depth-wm.csv records the projection distance.

nm000357.evidence: Other, mm; 'MNI152 template space as provided ... exact MNI152 template variant ... is not stated'; paper plots on MNI152NLin2009cAsym

sub-CS41/ses-P41CSR1/ieeg/sub-CS41_ses-P.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: MNI152 template space as provided by the data authors: the source writer reads the per-patient file macro_MNI.xyz and Keles et al. (2024) state that electrode locations are provided in MNI152 coordinates and visualised on the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template. The exact MNI152 template variant used to compute these values is not stated, so a specific template label is not asserted. Axes follow MNI convention (x right, y anterior, z superior), in mm. The per-column axis descriptions stored in the NWB electrodes table (e.g. "+x is posterior") are PyNWB defaults and do not describe these values. Electrodes with missing source coordinates are n/a. The authors note that some template-space locations fall in white matter due to misregistration; localisation was confirmed in native space, which is not distributed.
sub-CS41/ses-P41CSR1/ieeg/sub-CS41_ses-P.iEEGCoordinateProcessingDescription: Co-registration of pre-operative MRI with post-operative MRI and/or CT, then normalisation to MNI152 (source: Keles et al. 2024)

sub-10/ieeg/sub-10_coordsystem.json.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: x, y, z columns of the NWB electrodes table as released by the data authors. Zheng et al. (2024) state that each participant's preoperative MRI was aligned to the CIT168 template brain in MNI152 coordinates (affine followed by symmetric diffeomorphic normalisation) and report electrode MNI coordinates; the NWB columns carry no axis/space description, so a specific BIDS template label is not asserted. One coordinate per microwire bundle (all eight microwires of a Behnke-Fried electrode share the tip location; 'Each Behnke-Fried electrode shank had eight microwires on the tip and were marked as one anatomical location').

location.Description: Brain area of the microwire bundle as given in the NWB electrodes table (assigned by the data authors).

size.Description: Not documented per contact by the source (microwires are 40 µm diameter per the NWB device description).

sub-01/ieeg/sub-01_space-MNI152NLin6Asym.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: Values copied verbatim from the release file allContacts_MNIcoords.csv, described by the authors as coordinates 'in MNI 2mm standard space'. All values are positive integers (x 7-83, y 11-106, z 9-82), consistent with voxel indices of the FSL MNI152 T1 2 mm template (FSL MNI152_T1_2mm, i.e. MNI152NLin6Asym at 2 mm), not millimetres. They were not converted. If they are 0-based FSL voxel indices, millimetre coordinates follow from the template affine: x_mm = 90 - 2*x, y_mm = 2*y - 126, z_mm = 2*z - 72 (unverified assumption).
sub-01/ieeg/sub-01_space-MNI152NLin6Asym.iEEGCoordinateProcessingDescription: Authors' method (Dryad record): contact locations identified on post-operative CT and MRI, reconstructed in BioImage Suite, registered to the pre-operative MRI, converted from .MGRID to native-space coordinates with FieldTrip, written as a one-voxel-per-contact mask in FSL native space, and linearly registered to the MNI T1 2 mm standard brain.
sub-01/ieeg/sub-01_space-MNI152NLin6Asym.iEEGCoordinateProcessingReference: Sherman BE, Aljishi A, Graves KN, Quraishi IH, Sivaraju A, Damisah EC, Turk-Browne NB (2023). Intracranial entrainment reveals statistical learning across levels of abstraction. J Cogn Neurosci. doi:10.1162/jocn_a_02012

sub-311/ses-1/ieeg/sub-311_ses-1_space-O.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: Columns 2-4 of the authors' L_/R_MontageMap.mat, copied unchanged. The Dryad README calls them '3d MNI coordinates' and the article says BioImage Suite placed electrodes 'in MNI space (Colin 22 brain template)'. The values are all positive (about 10-200), i.e. image (voxel-index) coordinates in the template image rather than MNI millimetres, and the transform to MNI mm is not given. They are therefore NOT labelled MNI here; do not use them for atlas lookups without that transform.

on006890.evidence: Other, mm; relative 2D sheet-based system for monkey ECoG, left and right sheets independent

sub-monkeyb/ses-day09/ieeg/sub-monkeyb_s.iEEGCoordinateSystemDescription: Relative 2D sheet-based coordinate system. The monkeys were implanted with one ECoG electrodes sheet for each hemisphere (left: CH01-CH16; right: CH17-CH32). As no MRI, CT or intraoperative images were available, X and Y coordinates of each electrode were derived from the manufacturer's sheet design drawing, where z coordinates were set to 0. The origin was set at the first channel of each sheet (CH01 and CH17). Notably, because the relative position of the left and right sheets are unavailable, the coordinate systems for the left and right sheets are independent. The sheets were implanted so that CH01 and CH17 lie most posterior within their respective sheets. In essence, an increase in x and y values on the left sheet corresponds to an anterior and antero-left location in the brain, respectively. On the other hand, an increase in x and y values for the right sheet indicates more posterior and antero-left locations, respectively.
sub-monkeyb/ses-day09/ieeg/sub-monkeyb_s.iEEGCoordinateProcessingDescription: The electrode positions (x, y) were computed from the ECoG sheet design. The left and right sheets were handled independently, each with its own origin and coordinate axes. No coregistration with the subject's MRI/CT or standard space was performed.
